## `RestoreResult`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.RestoreResult` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

What one `Satone.RestoreDefaults` call did, per channel. The single `SATONE restore face=… motion=… gaze=…` console line is [`RestoreResult.Describe`](#restoreresult--describe).

"Scheduled" is the honest word for the expression: the game's own reset is `InitHeroineFacialAfterDelay(0.77f)` (`HeroineService` -&gt; `HeroineFacialController`), which waits before it writes `Facial = 0`. The gaze is the same shape - `LookInitSlowly()` eases out over 1.5 s after a half-second delay (`HeroineService` -&gt; `HeroineLookDirectionService`). Only the motion re-dispatch is immediate.

<a id="restoreresult--ctor"></a>

### `RestoreResult(RestoreScope requested, bool faceScheduled, float faceDelaySeconds, bool motionRedispatched, string motionState, string motionSkipReason, bool gazeReset, string problem, bool queued)`

Creates a result. Prefer the factories for the common shapes.

**Parameters**

- `requested`: The scope the caller asked for.
- `faceScheduled`: True when the expression reset was handed to the game.
- `faceDelaySeconds`: The delay that reset will wait, in seconds.
- `motionRedispatched`: True when the AI state was re-dispatched.
- `motionState`: The state that was (or would have been) re-dispatched.
- `motionSkipReason`: Why the motion was left alone; empty when it was not.
- `gazeReset`: True when the gaze ease-out was started.
- `problem`: Why nothing happened at all; empty when something did.
- `queued`: True when the call was queued for the next frame from another thread.

<a id="restorescope"></a>

## `RestoreScope`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.RestoreScope` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

Which of Satone's three mod-controlled channels a restore touches.

The game has no single "reset Satone" call. Each channel has its own idiom, and the game pairs them by hand at every site that changes her (for example `RoomGameManager.OnEndPlayedReaction`, `HeroineGameEndTalk.OnEnter:44-46`): expression -&gt; `InitHeroineFacialAfterDelay(0.77f)`, gaze -&gt; `LookInitSlowly()`, motion -&gt; re-dispatch the current AI state. This flags enum is how a caller says which of those three it wants.

The mouth is deliberately absent: `Enable_Talk` restores itself from the voice clip's completion callback (`HeroineVoiceController`).

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="restorescope--none"></a>`None` | 0 | Nothing. |
| <a id="restorescope--face"></a>`Face` | 1 | The expression - the Animator's `Facial` integer. |
| <a id="restorescope--motion"></a>`Motion` | 2 | The body motion - the Animator's `MotionType` integer. |
| <a id="restorescope--gaze"></a>`Gaze` | 4 | The gaze - the Animator's `LookScale` float and the IK look weight. |
| <a id="restorescope--all"></a>`All` | 7 | All three channels. |

## `SatoneCatalog`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneCatalog` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A parsed Satone table: every expression, body motion and AI state the game knows, with the name index that turns `"smile"` or `"10"` into the integer the game takes.

Immutable and Unity-free, so the whole naming contract is unit-testable off-engine. [`SatoneTable`](#satonetable) holds the one instance built from the embedded `satone-table.json`; [`SatoneCatalog.Parse`](#satonecatalog--parse) exists so a test (or a future pack override) can supply its own document.

A lookup tries three things, in order: the name or alias exactly (ordinal, case-insensitive), then the query as an integer id, then the name with separators removed ([`SatoneCatalog.LooseKey`](#satonecatalog--loosekey)) so the game's own `Wild001_Motion2_StretchShoulder` resolves as readily as the table's `wild001_motion2_stretch_shoulder`. A query that parses as an integer is never treated as a name - no row is named with digits alone.

Default number of names [`SatoneCatalog.Suggest`](#satonecatalog--suggest) returns.

<a id="satonecatalog--maxsuggestdistance"></a>

### `const int MaxSuggestDistance = 3`

Longest edit distance a name has to be within to be suggested at all.

<a id="satonecatalog--supportedschema"></a>

Schema version this code understands; a document that declares more is refused.

Verified collision-free over the generated table by `SatoneTableTests.LooseNamesAreCollisionFree`.

<a id="satonecatalog--suggest"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Suggest(string name, int max = 5)`

Canonical names close to `name`, best first, for a "did you mean" line.

Ranked: a name that starts with the query, then one that contains it, then one within [`SatoneCatalog.MaxSuggestDistance`](#satonecatalog--maxsuggestdistance) edits. Ties break on the shorter name and then alphabetically, so the same query always produces the same list.

**Parameters**

- `name`: What the caller typed. Null or blank returns an empty list.
- `max`: How many names at most. Values below 1 return an empty list.

## `SatoneFaceMeshes`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneFaceMeshes` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The face blendshapes one expression actually drives, grouped by family.

Satone's face is a single skinned mesh (`Character/Face`) with 47 blendshapes whose names start with `Eye_`, `Eyeblow_` (the game's spelling) or `Mouth_`. Every `anim_face_*` clip carries a curve for all of them and leaves most at zero, so the generator keeps only the shapes a clip pushes above zero. That is what makes two expressions comparable - `smile` and `fun` differ by exactly these lists.

**Parameters**

- `brow`: Blendshapes named `Eyeblow_*`.
- `mouth`: Blendshapes named `Mouth_*`.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy"></a>

## `SatoneRestorePolicy`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneRestorePolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Decides whether Satone's current AI state may be re-dispatched to put her body motion back on its base loop - the idiom the game itself uses after a click reaction (`HeroineAI.FinishHeroineClickReaction`, whose Work branch re-dispatches the current action state).

**Why an allow-list and not just a skip-list.** `StateMachineMonobehavior.Dispatch` re-enters the state it is already in - `Exit` then `Enter` - so re-dispatching runs the state's `OnEnter` again. That is exactly what we want for a work or break state, whose `OnEnter` sets a looping base motion (e.g. `HeroineStateWorkPC`, `HeroineStateBreakMovie`) and whose `OnUpdate` already pushes foreign motions back to it (`HeroineStateWorkPC`). It is wrong for every other state: the wild idles and the desk-to-desk transitions replay a one-shot clip (e.g. `HeroineStateWildGuts`, `HeroineStateFromPcToBook`), and the directed states restart a whole sequence.

The allow-list is exactly `HeroineAI.GetCurrentStateActionType`'s `Work` and `Break` members minus the three `LeaveChair*` states, which that method also counts as `Break` but whose `OnEnter` starts her walking away (`HeroineStateLeaveChairGoSofa`, `HeroineStateLeaveChairGoFar`).

Names are compared loosely, so both spellings of the same state work: the table's `work_pc` and the game's own enum member `WorkPC`.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--directed"></a>

### `static readonly IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> Directed`

The states that must never be re-dispatched, each with the reason a restore reports. A state that is in neither list is refused too, with the generic reason.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--notselfhealingreason"></a>

### `const string NotSelfHealingReason = "re-entering it replays a one-shot clip instead of restoring a loop"`

The reason given for a state that is in neither list.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--redispatchable"></a>

### `static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> Redispatchable`

The AI states whose `OnEnter` only re-arms a self-healing base loop, so re-dispatching them is a restore rather than a new performance.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--unknownstatereason"></a>

### `const string UnknownStateReason = "her AI state could not be named, so re-dispatching it is not safe"`

The reason given when the state name is empty or was never resolved.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--isdirected"></a>

### `static bool IsDirected(string stateName)`

True when `stateName` is one of the named directed sequences (as opposed to merely not being re-dispatchable).

**Parameters**

- `stateName`: The state, in either spelling.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--normalize"></a>

### `static string Normalize(string stateName)`

The comparison form of a state name: lower case with separators removed, so `work_pc`, `WorkPC` and `Work PC` are one key. Never null.

**Parameters**

- `stateName`: A state name, or null.

<a id="satonerestorepolicy--shouldredispatch"></a>

### `static bool ShouldRedispatch(string stateName, out string reason)`

Whether the body motion may be restored by re-dispatching `stateName`.

**Parameters**

- `stateName`: The state, in either spelling: the table's `work_pc` or the game's `WorkPC`. Null, empty or an `unknown_*` placeholder answers false.
- `reason`: Why not, when this returns false; `String.Empty` when it returns true. Never null - it is printed in the restore line.

**Returns:** True when re-dispatching the state restores rather than performs.

<a id="satonerevert"></a>

## `SatoneRevert`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneRevert` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: `IDisposable`

A scoped change to Satone: it remembers what she looked like before, and on [`SatoneRevert.Dispose`](#satonerevert--dispose) hands the channels it covers back to the game.

**Why it restores the game's default rather than the captured value.** The snapshot is kept for evidence, not for replay. Writing a captured `Facial = 18` back would be wrong outside the context that set it (`ScenarioReader` sets `Open_Eye` only while she is asleep), so the revert runs the game's own reset idiom - the same one `RoomGameManager.OnEndPlayedReaction` runs after a click reaction.

Engine-free: the actual restore is the delegate the adapter supplies. That delegate is expected not to throw (the adapter routes it through its main-thread host, which catches and logs), so nothing is swallowed here.

**Example**

```csharp
using (Satone.FaceScoped("smile"))
{
    // ... she smiles for as long as this block runs ...
}   // -> Satone.RestoreDefaults(RestoreScope.Face)
```

<a id="satonerevert--ctor"></a>

### `SatoneRevert(RestoreScope scope, SatoneSnapshot taken, Action<RestoreScope, SatoneSnapshot> restore)`

Creates a revert handle.

**Parameters**

- `scope`: The channels [`SatoneRevert.Dispose`](#satonerevert--dispose) restores.
- `taken`: What Satone looked like before the change.
- `restore`: What actually restores her, called once by [`SatoneRevert.Dispose`](#satonerevert--dispose). Null makes this a no-op handle, which is what a refused call returns.

<a id="satonerevert--disposed"></a>

### `bool Disposed { get; }`

True once [`SatoneRevert.Dispose`](#satonerevert--dispose) has run.

<a id="satonerevert--restores"></a>

### `bool Restores { get; }`

True when this handle will actually do something.

<a id="satonerevert--scope"></a>

### `RestoreScope Scope { get; }`

The channels this handle restores.

<a id="satonerevert--taken"></a>

### `SatoneSnapshot Taken { get; }`

What Satone looked like when the handle was taken.

<a id="satonerevert--dispose"></a>

### `void Dispose()`

Hands the covered channels back to the game. Idempotent: the second and later calls do nothing, so a `using` block inside a `finally` is safe.

<a id="satonerevert--none"></a>

### `static SatoneRevert None(RestoreScope scope = RestoreScope.None)`

A handle that restores nothing; returned when a call was refused.

**Parameters**

- `scope`: The scope the caller asked for, for the log line.

<a id="satonerevert--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

e.g. `revert face (facial=0 motion=200 look=0 state=work_pc)`.

<a id="satonesnapshot"></a>

## `SatoneSnapshot`

struct · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneSnapshot` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What Satone looked like at one instant: expression, body motion, gaze and the AI state that owns them. Taken before a change so the change can be described - and, where the values are readable, so a restore can be proved.

Every value is optional, because two of the three are read back through `UnityEngine.Animator` by reflection and that read-back is a diagnostic, not a guarantee: an unknown value is `null`, never a made-up 0. [`SatoneSnapshot.Diff`](#satonesnapshot--diff) therefore only reports a channel as changed when both snapshots know it.

Engine-free on purpose (anything worth a unit test lives in Core), so the capture rules can be tested without Unity.

<a id="satonesnapshot--ctor"></a>

### `SatoneSnapshot(bool valid, int? facialId, int? motionId, float? lookScale, int stateId, string stateName, double takenSeconds)`

Creates a snapshot.

**Parameters**

- `valid`: False when the room scope could not be read at all.
- `facialId`: The Animator's `Facial` integer, or null when unreadable.
- `motionId`: The `HeroineService.AnimationType` value, or null.
- `lookScale`: The Animator's `LookScale` float, or null when unreadable.
- `stateId`: The `HeroineAI.ActionStateType` value, or -1.
- `stateName`: Table name of the AI state, e.g. `work_pc`; null becomes empty.
- `takenSeconds`: A monotonic clock reading, for the log line.

<a id="satonesnapshot--defaultlooktolerance"></a>

### `const float DefaultLookTolerance = 0.05f`

How close two `LookScale` values count as the same by default.

<a id="satonesnapshot--unknown"></a>

### `static readonly SatoneSnapshot Unknown`

The "nothing is known" snapshot.

<a id="satonesnapshot--facialid"></a>

### `int? FacialId { get; }`

The `Facial` Animator integer, or null when the read-back is unavailable.

<a id="satonesnapshot--hasfacial"></a>

### `bool HasFacial { get; }`

True when the expression was readable.

<a id="satonesnapshot--haslook"></a>

### `bool HasLook { get; }`

True when the gaze was readable.

<a id="satonesnapshot--hasmotion"></a>

### `bool HasMotion { get; }`

True when the body motion was readable.

<a id="satonesnapshot--lookscale"></a>

### `float? LookScale { get; }`

The `LookScale` Animator float, or null when the read-back is unavailable.

<a id="satonesnapshot--motionid"></a>

### `int? MotionId { get; }`

The body motion the game last recorded, or null.

<a id="satonesnapshot--stateid"></a>

### `int StateId { get; }`

The `HeroineAI.ActionStateType` value, or -1 when it is not known.

<a id="satonesnapshot--statename"></a>

### `string StateName { get; }`

Table name of the AI state, e.g. `work_pc`. Never null.

<a id="satonesnapshot--takenseconds"></a>

### `double TakenSeconds { get; }`

Monotonic seconds at capture; 0 when nobody supplied a clock.

<a id="satonesnapshot--valid"></a>

### `bool Valid { get; }`

False when the snapshot could not be taken (no room scene, no service).

<a id="satonesnapshot--at"></a>

### `SatoneSnapshot At(double takenSeconds)`

This snapshot with a different capture time; everything else is kept.

**Parameters**

- `takenSeconds`: The new clock reading.

<a id="satonesnapshot--diff"></a>

### `RestoreScope Diff(SatoneSnapshot before, float lookTolerance = 0.05f)`

Which channels differ between `before` and this snapshot. A channel either side does not know is never reported as changed - "unknown" is not "different".

**Parameters**

- `before`: The earlier snapshot.
- `lookTolerance`: How far `LookScale` may drift before it counts as changed; the gaze is tweened, so an exact comparison would be noise. Negative values are treated as 0.

<a id="satonesnapshot--matches"></a>

### `bool Matches(SatoneSnapshot other, float lookTolerance = 0.05f)`

True when nothing this snapshot knows differs from `other`.

**Parameters**

- `other`: The snapshot to compare with.
- `lookTolerance`: See [`SatoneSnapshot.Diff`](#satonesnapshot--diff).

<a id="satonesnapshot--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

e.g. `facial=0 motion=200 look=0 state=work_pc`.

<a id="satonestate"></a>

## `SatoneState`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneState` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One member of the game's `HeroineAI.ActionStateType` - what Satone is currently doing (working at the PC, on a tea break, asleep, ...), as opposed to which clip is playing.

Read-only here. The state is owned by `HeroineAI.ChangeState` (private); the event bus already reports transitions, and this table exists so a name can be put on the number.

<a id="satonestate--ctor"></a>

Creates a row.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The enum value, -1 for `None`.
- `name`: snake\_case name, e.g. `break_tea_time`. Required.
- `actionStateType`: The `ActionStateType` member name. Required.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: A required name is null or blank.

<a id="satonestate--actionstatetype"></a>

The enum member name as the game spells it, e.g. `BreakTeaTime`.

The `HeroineAI.ActionStateType` value.

<a id="satonestate--name"></a>

snake\_case name, e.g. `break_tea_time`.

<a id="satonestate--tostring"></a>

<a id="satonetable"></a>

## `SatoneTable`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.SatoneTable` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The Satone table, embedded in this assembly: every expression, body motion and AI state of the game, named. This is what lets a mod write `Satone.Face("smile")` instead of `ChangeHeroineFacialAnimation(10)`.

The table lists the game's own facial, motion and state names (game 1.17.3); a game update that changes them needs a new table.

Loading is lazy, once, and never throws: a missing or broken resource leaves [`SatoneTable.Loaded`](#satonetable--loaded) false and [`SatoneTable.LoadError`](#satonetable--loaderror) set, and every query answers "no". The alternative - throwing out of a static constructor during a plugin's Awake - would take down the adapter for a data problem.

<a id="satonetable--resourcename"></a>

Name of the embedded resource this class reads.

Every expression, in id order.

True when the embedded table parsed.

<a id="satonetable--loaderror"></a>

### `static string LoadError { get; }`

Every body motion, in id order.

<a id="satonetable--states"></a>
